china_race_dynamics.text:
This week, my bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act is heading to the House floor.

America can beat China in the AI race without forcing families and small businesses to foot the bill for the massive energy demands of data centers.

I’m urging my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to support this commonsense bill and protect American ratepayers.

china_race_dynamics.text:
This issue is only becoming more important as the global race for artificial intelligence accelerates.

Communist China is working every day to outcompete the United States, wage cyberwar, steal American innovation and information, and expand its technological influence around the world. America cannot afford to lose that race.

deepseek.reason: The speaker says America cannot afford to lose the AI race against China and describes China as working to outcompete the US.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement explicitly endorses the AI race framing and competition priority.

china_race_dynamics.text:
American small businesses shouldn’t have to rely on Chinese Communist Party-linked AI models to compete.

My Open-Source AI Leadership Act promotes American alternatives while exposing the security risks posed by Chinese AI.

American data belongs in America — not in the hands of Communist China. We need to protect our innovators, our jobs, and our data. 🇺🇸

deepseek.reason: The speaker promotes American AI alternatives against Chinese models and frames reliance on CCP-linked AI as a competitive problem.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement explicitly frames Chinese AI as a competitive threat and endorses American alternatives.

china_race_dynamics.text:
America needs the digital infrastructure to win the AI race against Communist China — but Colorado families shouldn’t be forced to give up their water or pay higher utility bills to make it happen.

We can lead in AI AND develop data centers responsibly.

That’s why I introduced the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act to make sure the companies creating massive new electricity demand pay for the infrastructure they need — not Colorado families, farmers, seniors, and small businesses.

deepseek.reason: The speaker says America needs digital infrastructure to win the AI race against China while insisting data centers be developed responsibly and ratepayers protected.
deepseek.confidence_reason: Competition priority is explicit, but the safety-over-speed facet depends on reading responsible data-center and ratepayer safeguards as safeguards despite competitive pressure.

china_race_dynamics.text: The race for AI leadership is a race America cannot afford to lose. Communist China is working every day to outcompete us, steal American innovation, and expand its technological influence around the world. We should be making it easier for our nation's innovators and startups to build, compete, and lead. This bill helps unleash American open-source AI while implementing common sense consumer protections. It also creates safeguard to identify and counter national security threats from foreign adversaries.

china_race_dynamics.text:
I couldn’t agree more. America cannot afford to fall behind Communist China in the race for AI.

We need commonsense federal guardrails that protect Americans without crushing innovation.

That’s why I introduced the Open Source AI Leadership Act—to strengthen U.S. leadership in open source AI while identifying the risks posed by CCP-controlled models. ⬇️

china_race_dynamics.text: If you’re nervous about AI, you need to be terrified about communist China becoming the global leader in AI because it was driven out of places like Colorado as a result of Colorado’s AI law.

china_race_dynamics.text:
AI is a game changing technology, and there can be only one global leader. If America does not win the AI race, communist China will.

I joined @RepLangworthy in sending Howard Lutnick, the US Secretary of Commerce a letter highlighting concerns with burdensome state AI regulations, urging a coherent national framework that protects consumers without stopping innovation.

china_race_dynamics.text: Like it or not, artificial intelligence is here to stay. The U.S. can choose to lead the world in this transformative technology or we can regulate it into the hands of Communist China. If we care about American jobs, national security and staying ahead of our foreign adversaries, we need a smart, consistent national approach that keeps innovation here at home

china_race_dynamics.text: AI is poised to be among the most transformative technologies of our generation, with profound implications for American economic growth, competitiveness, and national security. The United States must lead in the development and deployment of these technologies, or we risk ceding future economic growth and global AI dominance to the Chinese Communist Party.
